claim_text: Gatwick says Times24, which runs its drop-off zones, had unauthorised access to AutoPay
summary: Gatwick Airport says it was told by Times24 UK, the company that manages its drop-off zones, that Times24 experienced unauthorised access to AutoPay, a third-party system that automatically charges drivers for dropping off.
detail: The airport has not said when the access happened or when it was found.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Gatwick spokesperson to the BBC: "We have been informed by Times24 UK Limited... that they experienced unauthorised access to AutoPay". The Register and The National carry the same statement.

claim_text: Names, addresses, contact details, AutoPay logins and vehicle details were reached
summary: Gatwick's email to customers says the data may include names, home addresses, postcodes, contact details, AutoPay logins, and registered vehicles with their entry and exit times. Most customers had only some of these exposed.
detail: The Register says the login details were email addresses and passwords stored in hashed form.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BBC: the data "included login credentials, email and home addresses, details of cars registered on the system"; The Register: "AutoPay login credentials such as email addresses and bcrypt-hashed passwords" and vehicle details.

claim_text: In a few cases, payment records and partial card details were reached
summary: The email says AutoPay payment records were reached, and in some isolated cases the card brand, the last four digits of the card number and its expiry date. Gatwick says the payment details apply only in very limited cases.
detail: No outlet reports that full card numbers were taken.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BBC: in some "isolated cases" the card brand, last four digits of the card number and expiry date were accessed; The Register: a Gatwick spokesperson said the payment records applied only in "very limited cases".

claim_text: AutoPay has been disabled; drivers can still use the drop-off zones and pay another way
summary: Gatwick says AutoPay has been disabled as a precaution; drivers can still use the drop-off zones and pay by another method on its website. The Register said on Nov 25 that AutoPay remained disabled while the investigation continued.
detail: Travel Radar (Nov 25-26) says Gatwick has not said when AutoPay will return. Gatwick's own website could not be read by the desk (it blocks automated readers).
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BBC, spokesperson: "the AutoPay system has been disabled." The Register: "The service remains disabled while the investigation continues." Travel Radar: Gatwick has not said when AutoPay will resume.

claim_text: Flights, car parks and the drop-off zones are working normally
summary: Gatwick says no flights were affected, its car parks are operating normally and the drop-off zones are still open.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BBC: "Gatwick said no flights had been affected" and "Car parks are also operating normally."; The Register: flights were unaffected and all other airport services are operating as usual.

claim_text: Gatwick has told affected customers and the Information Commissioner's Office
summary: Gatwick says the customers affected have been told by email and the UK's data protection regulator, the Information Commissioner's Office, has been informed. Outside cybersecurity specialists are helping.
detail: The National says customers were told on Monday, Nov 23.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BBC: "those who have been affected have been informed" and the ICO "has been informed"; The Register: outside cybersecurity specialists are helping; The National: Gatwick "told customers on Monday".

claim_text: Gatwick has not said how many customers were affected or how far back the records go
summary: Gatwick told The Register it could not say how many customers were affected or how far back the affected records go. Nobody has said when the access began.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Register: Gatwick "was unable to provide details about how many customers were affected... or how far back the affected records go." The National: "The airport did not reveal when the hack occurred".

claim_text: Nobody has been named as behind the access
summary: Gatwick and the outlets that reported it name no person or group behind the access, and no group has been reported claiming it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: None of the BBC, The Register or The National names an attacker or reports a claim of responsibility.

claim_text: The Register reports that AutoPay is operated by ParkPark and used by Times24
summary: The Register, from the customer email, says the affected system is AutoPay, operated by ParkPark and used by Times24 UK, Gatwick's drop-off zone manager.
detail: Times24's own website says it offers an Autopay service with a partner it names as Autopay Technologies. No source says whether that is the same company as ParkPark.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The Register: the email "identifies the affected system as AutoPay, operated by ParkPark and used by Gatwick's drop-off zone manager, Times24 UK Limited"; Times24: "We partner with Autopay Technologies".

claim_text: Times24 runs car parks across the UK, at airports, hospitals, universities and shops; no other site has said it was affected
summary: Times24, part of Japan's PARK24 group, says it runs car parks across a wide range of places, including airports, hospitals, universities and shops. No organisation other than Gatwick has said publicly that it was affected.
detail: The Register says Times24 operates more than 200 UK car parks and did not respond to its questions. Neither Times24 nor ParkPark has published a statement that the desk could find.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Times24: car park operations "across a wide range of sectors, including airports, hospitals, universities, retail settings and hospitality"; The Register: Times24 "operates across more than 200 car parks in the UK".

claim_text: Customers are told to be wary of messages that mention Gatwick or the drop-off payment
summary: The customer email warns people to be careful with unexpected emails, calls or texts, especially any from Gatwick, Times24, AutoPay or ParkPark that ask for payment or bank details.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: BBC: the email warns customers "to exercise caution when receiving unexpected emails, calls or text messages"; The Register: especially messages "that ask for payment or bank details".

claim_text: Gatwick is the UK's second-busiest airport
summary: London Gatwick, in Crawley, West Sussex, about 30 miles south of central London, was the UK's second-busiest airport by passengers in 2024, after Heathrow.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Wikipedia: Gatwick is "located in Crawley, in West Sussex, 30 miles south of Central London" and "In 2024, Gatwick was the second-busiest airport by total passenger traffic in the UK, after Heathrow".
